structured_output.hypothesis: If domestic dogs descended from several distinct wild species, then dog genomes should contain large, separable ancestry components that are each closest to a different wild Canis species, with deep divergence between those components.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using the dog reference assembly with assemblies and reads of gray wolf, coyote, golden jackal and other Canis species from NCBI, dog ancestry is polyphyletic across species. Specifically, at least 20% of non-overlapping 100-kb autosomal windows place dog sister to a non-wolf Canis species (coyote, jackal or others) with bootstrap support of at least 70%, AND the Patterson's D / f4 test for non-wolf introgression into dogs is significant (|Z| > 3) with an estimated non-wolf ancestry fraction of at least 20%.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Dog is monophyletic with gray wolf (Canis lupus) in at least 90% of supported windows (bootstrap of at least 70%). Non-wolf Canis ancestry in dogs is below 5% by f4-ratio/D-statistic, or not significant (|Z| < 3). Dog-wolf divergence is much shallower than any between-species divergence in Canis. Under these results the claim is refuted.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'distinct wild species' is read as separate extant or extinct species-level lineages in the genus Canis (for example wolf, jackal, coyote). The modern reading is that a species is a reproductively isolated, monophyletic lineage, so multiple species would show as deeply divergent ancestry components. Darwin's 'geographical and other considerations' are replaced by genome-wide phylogenetic and introgression statistics. Post-domestication gene flow from wolves or coyotes into dogs is regional and small. It must not be counted as descent from several species, so the thresholds require a large, genome-wide share. The test is run on genome data and does not recreate Darwin's morphological argument.

dataset.name: UU_Cfam_GSD_1.0 (Canis lupus familiaris) genome assembly, GCF_011100685.1
dataset.publisher: NCBI (National Center for Biotechnology Information), RefSeq / Assembly
dataset.why_it_fits: This is the NCBI RefSeq dog reference genome, with downloadable FASTA/GFF files and the NCBI Datasets API. Its Assembly records link to the wolf, coyote and jackal assemblies and to SRA read sets. Fields used: genomic FASTA sequence, 100-kb window alignments to other Canis assemblies, and species/taxon ID for each assembly (dog 9615 versus wolf, coyote and jackal). These allow window-based tree topology, D-statistic and f4-ratio tests of dog ancestry.
